intro.heading: Built on democrito
intro.body: democrito is an AI, atomic and agnostic design system based on token contracts, not just a component library. There are multiple ways to use democrito, from re-theme to complete re-make, so here we collect some of the applications shared by users.

systems.renamedNote: The --accent → --brand rename resolved a genuine collision: the authenticated portal inherited 54 shadcn primitives where --accent means 'neutral hover surface', while this codebase used it to mean 'the brand colour'. A usage sweep found ~26 uses meaning hover-surface and zero meaning brand. Rather than repoint either library, the project took --brand — a name neither claims. The cleanest example in the set of a contract break resolved by renaming rather than re-valuing.

systems.recipe: Take democrito's token architecture and directory taxonomy. Keep the storage format and the consumption contract exactly. Replace every value: desaturate the warm surfaces toward neutral, swap the terracotta accent for Andalucía green 127° away, drop to a single light theme. Rename the accent family to --brand to escape a shadcn collision, collapse the three-face type system to two by removing the licence-encumbered body face. Then write your own component layer against the tokens rather than restyling democrito's.

whatWeLearned.title: The contract travels further than the palette
whatWeLearned.body: Southern Startups shares no colour values with democrito, ships one theme instead of three, and wrote its own component layer — and is still recognisably the same system. What carried over was the three-tier token architecture, the storage format and the consumption rule. That, rather than the palette, is what a design system actually hands you.

whatWeLearned.title: Components survive a total palette replacement
whatWeLearned.body: habito replaced every colour with achromatic ramps and removed the accent hue outright. Every stock primitive that referenced only declared tokens kept rendering correctly — --accent resolved to a neutral and nothing complained. Inheriting the token names, not the values, is what makes that possible.
evidence: habito: 5 of 7 audited primitives byte-identical to stock

whatWeLearned.title: Declare every token your components reference
whatWeLearned.body: In Tailwind v4 a utility whose token is undeclared compiles to nothing — no error, the element inherits, and the result looks plausible. habito's sidebar.tsx is byte-identical to stock and renders transparent because seven --sidebar-* tokens were never declared. Nobody edited that component; the tokens simply weren't there. Worth a build-time check in any derived system.
evidence: southern-startups: 21 of 31 tokens absent or relocated

whatWeLearned.title: @theme-derived tokens need re-declaring to scope
whatWeLearned.body: Tailwind v4's @theme derives --color-* as hsl(var(--x)) and --radius-* as calc(var(--radius)…). A custom property's value is computed where it is declared — these are declared once at :root and freeze there, so overriding --background on a subtree changes nothing that bg-background reads. We hit this building the live vignettes on this page: all three rendered democrito's own palette until the derived names were re-declared on each wrapper too. Themeing a whole document is unaffected; scoping to part of one needs both layers.

whatWeLearned.title: Value format is part of the contract
whatWeLearned.body: democrito stores bare HSL triplets consumed as hsl(var(--x)). habito stores complete hsl() at a primitive tier. Both are defensible and they are not interchangeable — mixing them yields hsl(hsl(0 0% 98%)), which fails silently. Worth stating explicitly wherever a system documents its tokens.
evidence: habito: hsl() at primitive tier vs base bare triplets

whatWeLearned.title: The contract stops at the CSS boundary
whatWeLearned.body: Fonts, radius, spacing and type scales can reach components through tailwind.config.ts instead of custom properties. Anything supplied by config works fine in the app but cannot be re-scoped by CSS — which matters the moment a system needs an embedded or previewed surface.
evidence: prompt-x: three font families and the radius scale
southern-startups: radius scale as config literals
habito: spacing, type and shadows are Tailwind stock

whatWeLearned.title: Categorical colour deserves a documented carve-out
whatWeLearned.body: prompt-x added 21 hues to encode a nine-field domain model, and strength added a four-step effort ramp. Both read as departures from 'monochromatic + accent' — but democrito itself ships a nine-hue --category-* palette for exactly this purpose. Two of five systems reached for it, which says the principle needs to name categorical and semantic encoding as sanctioned rather than leaving it to inference.
